WKX design system

A local copy of the WKX Design System artifact in Claude, generated from system/, the source of truth.

OverviewColourTypeSpacing, radii, borders, sizes, glowsComponentsAssets

Overview

WKX is the shared look and feel of every WKX app: a calm console. A deep-navy night ground, hairline structure, condensed uppercase signage and mono data, with colour spent only on signal. Day is an equal light scheme, not an afterthought. The system fixes how things look; each app brings its own words.

Principles

  • Colour is signal. Neutrals carry the page. accent, caution and danger appear only where something has a state or an action. highlight marks what the reader is looking for: cross-referenced terms and filter matches.
  • Hairlines, not shadows. Structure is 1px line borders and dividers on flat surface panels. The only shadows are the glows on status lights and highlighted terms.
  • Three voices of type. Condensed uppercase for signage (labels, buttons, column heads), sans for prose, mono for anything a machine would recognise: identifiers, paths, numbers, times, commands.
  • Fluid, not boxed. The page takes the whole screen. Panels share rows as the screen widens, but prose stays capped inside them (prose-max).
  • Night and day. Follow the system setting, with an auto / light / dark override (ThemeToggle). Design every screen in both.

  • Put text in ink on ground, surface or surface-raised, and in ink-muted on any of them.
  • Use ink-strong sparingly: one headline per page, plus the big figures.
  • Spend accent once per view on a fill (the primary button). It can appear any number of times as a small status mark.
  • Never encode state by colour alone. Every status carries a word in the app's vocabulary beside its light or tone. Green and red differ mainly by hue, so the word does the work for colour-blind readers.
  • Show a source system's raw state verbatim beside your reading of it, e.g. "Source: ALARM. Status: settling". Don't soften it.
  • Contrast: every text token clears 4.5:1 on ground and surface in both themes, and ink-muted also on surface-raised. Keep accent, caution and danger text off surface-raised unless it is 19px bold or larger.

Type

  • Families: --font-condensed (Avenir Next Condensed), --font-sans (Avenir Next), --font-mono (Menlo / SF Mono). These are macOS system faces with standard fallbacks; no web fonts are loaded.
  • Signage: headline, title, section-label, button-label, column-head and stat-key are condensed, always UPPERCASE, and tracked from 0.1em to 0.24em. The smaller the label, the wider the tracking.
  • Prose: body (15px / 1.5) and note in ink; lede and caption in ink-muted. Bold words in a muted line step up to ink, weight 600.
  • Data: figure, data, data-sm, meta and log are mono. Use font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums wherever digits line up.
  • Writing: NZ English, sentence case for prose and buttons (buttons are uppercased by style). Put a space between a number and its unit (6 %, 1.7 / 3.8 GiB, 4 h 38 m). Join metadata with · . Use → for a change from one value to another. Write dates as 18 Jul 14:32 and give the time zone once, in the page head.

Layout and spacing

  • Gutter: fluid, clamp(1.5rem, 2.5vw, 4rem) each side, with 5rem at the foot of the page.
  • Panel: space-4 padding on top and space-5 on the sides and bottom. Grid gap space-6; between major sections space-7.
  • Inside rows: space-1 from label to control, space-2 for tight pairs, space-3 between columns.
  • Grid: two columns, stacking below breakpoint-stack (860px). From breakpoint-wide (1500px), half panels share a six-column row; from 2100px, small panels go three-up.
  • Radii: radius-lg for panels and legends, radius-md for controls and wells, radius-sm for meters, radius-xs for highlighted terms and filter matches, radius-pill for pill controls (the table filter and columns menu), and radius-full only for status lights. A panel with a top rule (border-rule) keeps its top corners square.

Page anatomy

  1. Page chrome: a mono strip with the app name on the left and ThemeToggle on the right.
  2. Head: the headline (ink-strong; an optional second word at weight 500 in ink-muted), a mono timestamp right-aligned, a lede under it, then a Legend if the page shows status.
  3. Groups: ruled Panels, one per top-level grouping (place, environment, account), each a list of ListRows. A group with nothing in it says so plainly with an off light.
  4. Console: a .wkx-grid of panels, each opening with a SectionLabel, holding Gauges, DataTables, LogViews and finally a panel of actions (Button, Field).

States, motion and focus

  • Status lights: good and caution lights breathe on a 3.2 s cycle; danger holds still; off is an empty ring. All motion stops under prefers-reduced-motion.
  • Hover: control borders step from line to ink-muted. The primary button moves to accent-hover, and the danger button gains danger-tint.
  • Focus: every focusable thing gets a 2px solid caution ring at a 2px offset, which clears 3:1 on every surface in both themes. Never remove it.
  • Empty states: state what is missing and when it is expected, in a note, beside an off light.

Iconography

State is shown with status lights and words, and structure with hairlines and signage. The only mark is assets/Logos/wkx-mark.svg, which is also the favicon.

Components

Button

Actions

The one control style: condensed, uppercase, tracked, on a 4px radius.

Use default for most actions, primary (an accent fill) at most once per view for the action the view exists for, and danger (an outline in danger) for anything destructive. Use size="small" inside panel footers.

Consumer provides the label as children (a verb first, plus the exact object where it matters: "Deploy e7d09b4", "Roll back to a3f91c2"), onClick, and any native button props. type defaults to button.

Don't fill a danger button, add icons, or put two primaries side by side.

StatusLight

Status

An 11px lit disc that shows state at a glance: good, caution, danger or off.

Good (accent) and caution (caution) breathe slowly; danger (danger) holds still so it reads as urgent, not ambient; off is an empty ring for something reserved or not running. Breathing stops under prefers-reduced-motion.

Consumer provides status and an accessible label naming the state in the app's own words (it defaults to the status name).

Always pair a light with a word nearby. Green and red differ by hue more than lightness, so the light alone is not enough for colour-blind readers.

SectionLabel

Structure

The signature section head: a short rule, an uppercase condensed label in ink-muted, and a rule running to the edge.

Use it to open every panel and page section. Pass code for a machine identifier (a path, a resource name), set in mono ink ahead of the label; the two are joined by · .

Consumer provides the label as children, optionally code.

Don't use it for headings inside running prose, or stack two in a row.

Panel

Structure

The container for one job on a page: surface fill, a 1px line border, 6px corners, no shadow.

Variants. Default panels open with a SectionLabel (label, optional labelCode). A ruled panel carries a 3px ink-muted top rule with square top corners and a mono title plus aside head: use it for top-level groups, such as one per environment or location.

Layout. Put panels in a .wkx-grid (two columns, space-6 gap, stacking below 860px); wide spans the full row. On wide screens, let more panels share a row rather than stretching prose: keep prose under prose-max.

Consumer provides children, and label or title.

Don't nest panels, add shadows, or colour a panel's border by status: status lives in lights and words.

Gauge

Data

A key, a big mono figure with its unit, one line of detail, and an optional Meter.

Use in a .wkx-gauges row (four-up, two-up below 860px) for the handful of numbers someone checks first. The figure is ink-strong; the unit and detail drop to ink-muted.

Consumer provides label, value (a string, already formatted), unit, detail, and for a meter percent (0–100), threshold (where the tick sits) and tone (good, caution, danger) chosen by the app from that threshold.

Write a space between a number and its unit (6 %, 4 h 38 m), and say what the figure means in the detail line rather than repeating the key.

Meter

Data

A 6px track in surface-raised with a fill and a hairline threshold tick.

Tone is the app's judgement, not the meter's: pass good (default, accent), caution or danger once the value crosses the line you care about, and place threshold at that line so the reader can see the margin.

Consumer provides value (0–100), optional threshold (0–100), tone and an accessible label.

DataTable

Data

A mono table with condensed uppercase column heads and hairline row dividers, which can sort by any column, filter its rows and hide columns.

Use for event histories and records people scan by column. Write the outcome as a word and tone it good, caution or danger; tone timestamps and notes muted so the identifiers stand out.

Sort. With sortable, each column head is a button. A click sorts ascending (▲), then descending (▼), then returns the rows to the order you gave. The sorted head steps up to ink and carries aria-sort; on any other head the triangle shows faintly on hover or focus. Numbers sort as numbers, words in natural order, and blanks (—, ·) go last either way. Mark number columns num so they right-align.

Filter. With filterable, a pill sits above the table on the right. A row stays when any visible cell's text contains the filter, ignoring case, and each match in a plain-text cell is marked with highlight. The N of M count appears to the left of the pill, so the pill never moves as you type. When nothing matches, the table says so in one muted row.

Columns. With hideable, a columns ▾ pill sits to the right of the filter and drops a checklist of the columns. A locked column stays shown, and the last visible column can't be hidden. A hidden column is outside the filter's reach. The menu closes on a click outside it or Escape.

Sticky heads. The column heads stick to the top of the screen as a long table scrolls past, on a surface ground. Under a fixed page header, set stickyTop to its height. Below breakpoint-stack the table scrolls sideways inside its own wrapper instead.

Consumer provides columns ({key, label, num?, sortable?, locked?}), rows (objects keyed by column, with optional id, tones, sorts and search per row), and an optional caption. Give sorts when a cell's text does not sort right (a date shown as 18 Jul 14:32), and search when a cell is not plain text. To keep sort, filter or hidden columns across visits, control them with sort / onSortChange, filter / onFilterChange and hidden / onHiddenChange; otherwise set defaultSort, defaultFilter and defaultHidden.

Don't zebra-stripe, box cells, or centre text. Don't filter a table of a handful of rows: the pill earns its place at about a dozen. Put a table in a Panel, so its sticky heads match the ground behind them.

ListRow

Data

One item in a list: a status light, a mono name with a muted detail line beneath, and a right-aligned stat.

Use for inventories (services, jobs, devices). Rows divide with hairlines; the last has none.

Consumer provides status, statusLabel (optional, the state in words), name, detail and stat (it shows · when absent).

Field

Inputs

A labelled text input: the label is mono ink-muted above an inset (ground) input with a 4px radius.

Use a machine-readable label when the field edits a named setting (its key or path); otherwise a short plain label. Sit fields in a row with the button that commits them, bottoms aligned.

Consumer provides label, id (stable, for form restoration), and any native input props (value/onChange or defaultValue).

Highlight

Interaction

Cross-reference highlighting: a dotted underline marks a term; hovering or focusing it fills every occurrence on the page with highlight, clicking or Enter pins it, and Escape releases.

Use for the terms people trace across panels: names, environments, identifiers. Mark every occurrence, or the feature lies. Pair it once per page with WKX.Hint, the pale chip that explains the gesture.

Consumer provides the visible text as children and a term key when several spellings should light together.

Don't mark ordinary words. highlight also marks filter matches in DataTable; keep it to marking what the reader is looking for.

Legend

Status

A key strip under the page head that teaches the status lights once: light, the app's word for the state, and what it asks of the reader.

Consumer provides items ({status, term, meaning}), with term in the app's own vocabulary; the system fixes only the light for each status (good, caution, danger, off).

Use one per page, near the top, whenever the page shows more than one status.

LogView

Data

A mono log in an inset ground well that follows new lines to the bottom.

Use for streams people glance at: request logs, job output. Colour only the parts that carry state (status codes good, caution, danger) and mute timestamps and timings. Offer Pause in the footer for any live stream.

Consumer provides lines ({id, time, parts: [{text, tone}]} or {text}), height (default 11.5rem), follow (default true), label and an optional footer.

ThemeToggle

Interaction

A small mono button that cycles auto, light and dark.

Night (dark) is the identity; day (light) is its equal. Auto follows the system setting and tracks changes; light and dark override it and persist in localStorage when storage is allowed. It sets data-theme on <html>, which is what the tokens key on.

Use one per app, top right of the page chrome.

Consumer provides an optional storageKey (default wkx-theme) and label={false} to drop the "theme:" prefix.

Apps should also apply a saved override before first paint, so there is no flash.

Assets

Logos

wkx-mark.svg is the app mark and favicon: a pale-yellow (highlight, #FFE9A3) slash on a near-navy (ground Night, #0A141E) square. It is fixed-colour and reads on both themes; use it as the favicon of every WKX app. There is no wordmark: set the name in the headline style.
